title: Complete Blood Count: Indices, Histograms, and Flags
summary: One-paragraph overview used in cards and search results: the CBC reports red cell, white cell, and platelet measurements plus derived indices (MCV, MCH, MCHC, RDW) that classify anemias and flag results needing manual review.
objectives: Calculate and interpret MCV, MCH, MCHC, and RDW.
Use red cell indices to classify microcytic, normocytic, and macrocytic anemias.
Recognize instrument flags that require a peripheral smear review.

highYield: MCV < 80 fL suggests microcytic anemia; MCV > 100 fL suggests macrocytic anemia.
RDW is elevated in iron deficiency but usually normal in thalassemia trait.
A platelet count must be confirmed on a smear when the histogram or flag suggests clumping.

rows: SD or CV of RBC volume

quickReview.mnemonic: MCV is the siZe index, MCH the weight, MCHC the concentration.

deepStudy.introduction: The CBC is the most ordered laboratory test. Understanding how each parameter is measured — and which preanalytical issues distort it — turns a printout into a diagnosis.

sections.heading: Red cell indices
sections.body: Indices are calculated, not directly measured: MCV = Hct/RBC, MCH = Hb/RBC, MCHC = Hb/Hct. They classify anemia size and hemoglobinization; RDW separates iron deficiency (high RDW) from thalassemia trait (normal RDW).

sections.heading: Flags and histograms
sections.body: Automated analyzers produce RBC, WBC, and platelet histograms plus flags (e.g., RBC agglutination, platelet clumps, blast flag). Flags are prompts for a manual differential and smear review, not diagnoses.

deepStudy.clinicalSignificance: Microcytosis with high RDW suggests iron deficiency; microcytosis with normal RDW suggests thalassemia trait. Macrocytosis prompts B12/folate review and alcohol/liver history.
deepStudy.labInterpretation: Cold agglutinins falsely raise MCV and MCHC and lower RBC count; sample warming and saline replacement resolve this. Reference intervals vary by laboratory, method, age, sex, and population; verify against your local laboratory.
examTraps: MCHC above ~36 g/dL usually signals interference (lipemia, cold agglutinins, hemolysis) rather than a real value.
A normal MCV does not exclude iron deficiency early on; check ferritin and RDW.

memoryHooks.text: RDW high = variety (iron deficiency); RDW normal = uniform (thalassemia trait).
memoryHooks.funny: Bantay-sarado ang RDW: 'pag mataas, may variety show ng sizes; 'pag normal, pare-parehas lang sila ng sukat — boring pero classic thal trait.

references.title: Henry's Clinical Diagnosis and Management by Laboratory Methods
